newsitem.title: USA: Two deny extortion bid on model Elle MacPherson.
newsitem.headline: Two deny extortion bid on model Elle MacPherson.

text.p: Two men accused of threatening to put nude photographs of supermodel Elle MacPherson on the Internet unless she paid them thousands of dollars pleaded not guilty on Tuesday to attempted extortion.
Michael Mishler, 29, and William Holt, 26, are alleged to have sent threatening letters to MacPherson demanding $80,000 to keep the all-revealing pictures off the information super highway.
Prosecutors claim Mishler stole the pictures -- which MacPherson says she took of herself for a book she was working on -- from the model's home on exclusive Mulholland Drive.

During Tuesday's brief, two-minute hearing Mishler pleaded innocent to charges of burglary, attempted extortion, writing a threatening letter for the purpose of extortion and being a felon in possession of a firearm.
Holt pleaded not guilty to one count of attempted extortion. Both men are being held on bail of $300,000 and appeared in court handcuffed and wearing blue prison jumpsuits.
Prosecutors allege Mishler hatched the plot to blackmail MacPherson and Holt was his willing accomplice.
Police claim Mishler broke into MacPherson's house and a trailer she owned and stole the photographs. The two then sent letters threatening the model and actress unless she paid up.
MacPherson informed police and the pair were arrested when they picked up the money left by her at a pre-arranged drop spot inside a Beverly Hills shopping mall.

But Mishler's attorney, Lawrence Young, has said his client and MacPherson were romantically involved and that Mishler was the statuesque model's "boy toy." The phrase is generally used to describe a much younger male escort. At 33, MacPherson is four years older than Mishler.
Young has insisted his client is innocent though conceding Mishler took "rash actions" after being jilted by "one of the most beautiful women in the world."
Mishler, Young has told reporters, was a frequent visitor to MacPherson's home and she gave him the photographs and other belongings.

MacPherson, who is in the current movie, "Batman and Robin," claims she does not know either of the defendants and denied any sort of relationship with Mishler. She has sued Young over his "boy toy" remarks, which the lawyer made to reporters in public.

She told a news conference last month that she had taken the nude photographs herself using a camera with a timer. She also claimed she had lost about $100,000 in jewellery and cash in the June 12 burglary allegedly committed by Mishler.
